hypothesis.statement: On real WBDS knee-angle gait cycles across 8 treadmill speeds (42 subjects, within-subject centred), function-on-scalar regression recovers the established speed-dependence of the knee: the speed-coefficient curve is significant (curve-wide permutation p<0.001), positive, and peaks at the swing-flexion (~65% cycle) at ~+3.3 deg per speed level; pooled peak knee flexion rises with speed (r~0.63).

analysis_plan.dataset: WBDS (figshare 5722711), 42 adults x 8 treadmill speeds; sagittal RKneeAngleZ over the gait cycle (101 pts); 328 subject-speed curves

decision.threshold: descriptive: the pointwise speed-coefficient curve (deg per speed level) + its curve-wide permutation p; the coefficient should be significant (p<0.05), positive at its peak, and peak in the swing phase (55-75% cycle), with peak flexion rising with speed (r>0.4)
